Deﬁnition
Debris size: 10x5x5cm (0.1x0.05x0.05m):
■ Debris objects must be at least 10cm along one axis (length, height, width), and at least 5cm along the other
two axis.
■ Non-debris objects do not need to conform to this minimal size (for example, small Animals).
Dynamic Debris:
■ Dynamic debris are scattered objects of trash that are found in or near the street.
■ Dynamic debris are objects that are light weight and can move on their own by rolling or wind.
■ Can usually be driven over by the AV.
■ Examples: plastic bags, paper cups, empty boxes, blankets, glass bottles, or any other waste objects
Static Debris:
■ Static debris are objects of signiﬁcance on or near the street.
■ Static debris are objects that are heavy in weight and can not move on their own.
■ Cannot be driven over by the AV.
■ Examples: boulders, crates, boxes that are not empty, car tires, cinderblocks, mattress, or other large, heavy
objects

Labeling Standards
■ Turn on the ground lidar toggle.
■ Dynamic Debris is to be labeled everywhere.
■ debris in the road should use the debris attribute toggle.
■ debris on the sidewalk, that might interact with the AV, is labeled as a dynamic obstacle
with the debris attribute toggle.
■ debris on the sidewalk, that will not interact with the AV, is labeled as a dynamic obstacle
and no debris attributes.
■ Static Debris is to be labeled everywhere.
■ debris in the road should use the debris attribute toggle.
■ debris on the sidewalk should be labeled as a static obstacle and no debris attributes.
■ Static debris does not move on its own and therefore if on the sidewalk, it will
not interact with the AV
■ Piles of debris:
■ If there is less than a 5cm gap between objects they should be grouped into one large
object.
■ If there is a large gap between the objects, they should be labeled individually.
■ Construction Areas:
■ Construction equipment, cones, and posts are not to labeled as debris.
■ Debris in construction areas should be labeled.

The following are all attributes that can be applied to an object of this class in Gulp. See the example section for examples of each attribute. See

Debris_is_empty - Indicates whether or not a piece of debris is occupied with other objects. This attribute is applied to objects that are

■ True - the debris container is not occupied with other objects
Debris_can_drive_over - Indicates whether or not debris can be driven over.
■ False - indicates that the debris can not be driven over (usually a static obstacle)
■ Unknown - there is no indicator to know if the debris can be driven over
■ True - indicates that the debris can be driven over (usually a dynamic obstacle)

Deﬁnition
■ A person is a human being.
■ They are typically no taller than 2.5 meters.
Labeling Standards
■ All person objects will need to have posture time varying attribute (TVA).
■ All persons need to be assigned a VRU size.
■ The reﬂective vest attribute is used when a person, e.g construction worker, is wearing a
bright orange or yellow reﬂective jacket, or vest.
■ If a stroller is present assume there is a person inside. Animals in strollers are also
treated as a humans.
■ If a person is controlling traﬃc with a sign, the person and sign each get their own
bounding box.
■ Label dolls as a small VRU. If a doll is being carried it can be labeled as part of the
person.
■ Objects attached to or being carried by a person can be ignored with a few exceptions.
■ Do not label persons inside of vehicles or buildings.
■ Do not label a person's extremities that are sticking out of vehicles.
■ Do not label pictures of people on buses, billboards, or art.

Time Varying Attributes (TVAs) for this Class
Person Posture TVA - refers to the state at which each person's posture resembles
■ Dismounting - Applies when the person is dismounting from a personal vehicle (i.e., bicycles,
motorcycles, or portable vehicles).
■ Falling - Applies to a person showing signs of falling or losing their balance until the person falls
completely to the ground.
■ Lying - Applies to a person that is lying when the back or chest, rear-end, both legs, or both knees are
on the ground. Alternatively if a person is in the act of falling, a person can be considered lying if at
least one of their knees or legs, along with at least one hand is touching the ground and they are not
actively trying to get up.
■ Other - Applies when any other posture that is not normal, lying, falling, or dismounting.
■ Unknown - Applies when the person is not visible (occluded) for an extended number of frames.
■ Normal - Applies to people standing, walking, or sitting in a chair. It also applies to bicycles,
motorcycles, or portable vehicles (skateboards, scooters, roller skates) riding or stationary.

Relationships for this Class
is controlled by - Used within an object relationship to indicate the object that is being pushed, pulled, or controlled, by
another object.
■ controls - Used within an object relationship to indicate the object that is pulling, or controlling,
another object.
■ When a person is pushing or pulling an object, they are controlling that object.
■ That same object is being controlled by the person.
■ made by - Used within an object relationship to indicate the object has made, or caused, another object.
■ If a person jumps into a puddle and makes a splash, the splash is made by the human.

Deﬁnition
■ Static obstacles are objects that cannot be freely moved without assistance from a person or vehicle.
■ Examples: traﬃc light poles, bus stops, utility structures, stationary dumpsters, hydrants, collection boxes, tents, covered
vehicles, vegetation planters, porta potties, scaﬀolding, other miscellaneous heavy objects or debris, and posts that are
wider than they are tall.
Cruise Internal: In GT Uniﬁed Taxonomy, the term static deviates from the kinematic deﬁnition which may be used by other internal
teams. In GT, static obstacles are objects which cannot move, whereas dynamic obstacles are objects which can move of their own
volition.
Labeling Standards
■ Chain link fences are to be labeled as static obstacles and can be labeled as one long bounding box.
■ Parked and fully covered motorcycles and vehicles are static obstacles due to not being able to be safely driven.
■ Racks that hold bicycles are also static obstacles whereas the bicycles themselves are bicycles.
■ Static objects in constructions areas may receive the construction attribute.
■ Traﬃc light posts only needs to be labeled in lidar. Refer to Traﬃc Lights Taxonomy for more information.
■ Posts that are wider than they are tall, or have the same width and height dimensions, are static obstacles.
